findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The dish machine in the kitchen was observed to have Laundry Chlorine Bleach hooked up to it and was only heat sanitizing at 146F. The PIC called EcoLab regarding this issue. The EcoLab representative has ordered a part to repair the dish machine, as it is not properly reaching a heat sanitizing temperature of 165F or above. The Laundry Chlorine Bleach was disconnected from the machine, as this was the wrong chemical delivered by US Foods. The EcoLab representative explained that the dish machine does not always properly reach the heat sanitizing temperature needed due to heavy usage and not having a booster directly on the machine, therefore, there is an ultra-sanitizer chemical hooked up to the machine to ensure that it is sanitizing dishes. The PIC will be obtaining this chemical to ensure that it is sanitizing. Ensure that this dish machine is not used until this chemical is obtained and is properly sanitizing at the label-recommended concentration. 

The Chlorine sanitizing dish machine in the bar area is observed to have an “Out of Order” sign on it and a part has been ordered for it. The facility has been bringing the bar dishes to the kitchen to be cleaned. 

A follow up is scheduled on 12/8/2025 to ensure that the kitchen dish machine has been repaired and is properly sanitizing. A spot check will be conducted when the bar dish machine has been repaired to ensure that it is properly sanitizing.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: FIRST REPEAT- There was a gallon of milk observed to not have any date marking on it. CORRECTED- The PIC was unsure of when the milk was opened and the milk was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that all TCS food prepared and held in an establishment for more than 24 hours is marked with the date of preparation or opening and is discarded on the end of the 7th day. 

 (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Observed the bar dish machine to be at 0 ppm chlorine. Ecolab serviced the dish machine during the inspection, and according to operator the sanitizer has been "gassed", turning the solution from yellow to clear indicating all chlorine has evaporated. Ecolab repaired the machine during the inspection which tested at 100 ppm chlorine. Mechanical dish machines shall be maintained to provide proper chemical sanitizing concentrations. Use test kits to confirm solution concentration. 750-830

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
1) Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting next to the prep sink in the kitchen and the sanitizer bucket next to it to test at 0 ppm quat. Sanitizer bucket was replaced with one testing at 200 ppm quat. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use. 2). Observed wiping cloths sitting on the three compartment sink and counter next to clean glasses in the bar area.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the soda gun nozzle behind the bar to be soiled and sticky. Wash, clean, and sanitize the soda gun nozzle behind the bar area. 2) Observed the can opener blade in the bakery area to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris and some rust. Remove rust or replace blade. Wash, rinse, and sanitize this food contact surface after each use or if it is being used on a continual basis, wash, rinse, and sanitize at least once every four hours.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed a 5 gallon bucket that is used to help drain the tilt to be soiled with food debris buildup. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
1) Observed a mop bucket with black, dirty mop water in it sitting in the dish room. Properly discard all wastewater after use. Mop water was discarded during inspection.
750-1130(e) Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
1). Observed the three compartment sink in the dish room hot water handle appears to be broken and continuous leak from the faucet. Repair plumbing.
2) Observed a soda gun holder at the bar to have the drain line disconnected from plumbing. Ensure drain is properly draining. This area is an ideal breeding ground for fruit and drain flies.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
1). Observed no paper towel at the hand sink behind the coffee area. Provide paper towel at the hand sink in the coffee area. 2). Observed no soap at the hand sink near the three compartment sink behind the bar. Provide soap at the hand sink behind near the three compartment sink behind the bar.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 1). Observed several drain flies in the two hand sinks and three compartment sink in the bar area. Flies appeared to be breeding in soda gun holder and connected drain line which is no longer connected to plumbing and not properly draining. Treat bar area and rest of kitchen for fruit flies. Eliminate food and water source for pest. Pay special attention to drains. A follow up inspection will be conducted on May 2, 2016.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) Observed the soda syrup room to have the floor heavily soiled with soda syrup from a leak of a soda syrup box. 2) Observed the soda syrup room to not be properly coved. A large gap between the wall in floor joint is apparent and has accumulated debris. Clean wall to floor joint and provide coving to eliminate accumulation of debris in this uncleanable area.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 1) Observed holes in the wall above the mop sink in the dish room needs to be caulked. Caulk the holes in the wall above the mop sink in the dish room. 2) Observed the wall behind the soda syrup boxes where a leak has recently occurred to be damaged and soiled due to the soda syrup spill. The lower area of the dry wall has began to absorb the soda syrup. Clean wall as much as possible and if soda syrup is not able to be removed, replace area of damaged dry wall. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings. 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed the light shield above the dish machine to be missing. Replace shield or provide shatterproof bulbs.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed two coats in the dish machine room to be stored on the corner of shelving used to store clean equipment. Properly store all personal belongings away from food, food equipment, or food preparation areas.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed green liquid in a spray bottle store with other toxic items on the bottom shelf underneath the three compartment sink with no label. Bottle was properly labeled to correct violation.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed containers of ham, turkey, pulled pork, and eggs to be dated 12/17. Date marking and limiting foods to 7 days was discussed with staff. Items were discarded to correct the violation. 750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Observed the dish machine at the bar to me at improper chemical sanitizing concentrations. Dish machine was ran and tested multiple times. Unit tested at ~10 ppm chlorine. Ecolab was called to service the dish machine during the inspection. Violation is considered corrected. Use test kits throughout the day to ensure dish machine is at proper sanitizing concentrations. Dish machine was re-tested and is now at 50 ppm chlorine. 750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the blade guard of the deli slicer in the pantry area to have an accumulation of food debris. Wash, rinse, and sanitize these food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.comment:

Wash. rinse, and sanitize this bulk food container.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

findings.comment:
1) CORRECTED> Observed a container of moldy strawberries in the reach in cooler in the bar. Strawberries were discarded during inspection. Provide wholesome foods. 
CORRECTED> 2) Observed 5 heavily dented cans in dry storage room. Cans were discarded to correct the violation. Check cans for sound condition. Any cans with dents along the horizontal or vertical seams shall be discarded or segregated from canned goods in sounded condition and returned to distributor. 750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> 1) Observed two open milk gallons in the banquet walk in cooler that were not date marked. Milk was discarded during inspection. CORRECTED> 2) Observed a container of au jus dated 8/1 and container of meatballs with no date in refrigerator. CORRECTED> 3) Observed two plates of cooked breakfast sausages in lowboy cooler on the cook line with no date marking. CORRECTED> 4) Tray of chicken and tray of spaghetti left in the non-operational blast chiller over night. Items were at 64F. Items were discarded to correct all violations.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Pantry hand sink is pulling away from the wall and a gap is visible between top of sink and wall joint. Seal gap.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:

750-830c A thermometer ±3°F shall be provided to check the temperature of  the water in each tank of the dish machine and the temperature of  the final rinse water as it enters the manifold.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
1) Observed no time marking on a container of rice in cooler #6 which just began the cooling process. Rice was at 120F and according to staff, the item was only out of temperature control for ~15-20 minutes. The cooling process and time marking was discussed at length with the chef and staff. Item was properly time marked and moved into the walk in cooler.
2) Multiple items throughout the facility which identities are not easily known and unlabeled. Train staff to label all foods unless their identities are unmistakable. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. 750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed the following items in the prep cooler above cooler #6 to be at improper temperatures: swish cheese (58F), ham  (55F), shell eggs (55F), diced ham (56F). Items were probed with a recently calibrated stem thermometer. Items were voluntarily discarded to correct the violation. Maintain potentially hazardous foods which require refrigeration at 41F or below.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)
